description: Build your dream mountain home on this exceptional southwest-facing homesite in Couch Mountain, where long-range mountain views, abundant natural light, and spectacular sunsets create an unforgettable setting. This private lot backs up to conserved land and is framed by mature hardwoods, offering both beauty and lasting privacy. Three unique rock formations provide opportunities to create a distinctive driveway entrance, landscape feature, or architectural focal point. Additionally, several attractive boulders near the front of the property were intentionally placed there for future landscaping and garden design. Inspired by traditional Japanese garden "rock setting" techniques, these stones were selected and relocated to the site rather than naturally emerging from the ground. The lot has already been cleared for site work, soil testing is complete, and it is approved for a 4-bedroom septic system. A gentle slope offers flexibility for a walkout basement, crawl space, or single-level home design. A builder has performed an initial evaluation in 6 excavated test pits in the proposed building envelope and determined that surface rock was removed without the need for drilling. A 2-foot topographic survey is available, and underground power is already in place. Chickens and bees are permitted. Residents enjoy access to a 138-acre nature preserve, private hiking trails, a mountaintop park, community gardens, greenhouse, vegetable stand, and apiaries. Conveniently located between Asheville and Hendersonville, you'll enjoy easy access to dining, outdoor recreation, and everything Western North Carolina has to offer. A rare opportunity to build in a mountain community that blends natural beauty, privacy, and connection to the land.

description: It's been a year since we settled in and my back deck has slowly become my favorite room in the house. My three-bedroom home is nothing showy around 1400 sq.ft., but the walk out basement is full of light, and we love to spend the cool evenings on the back porch. Most mornings I'm out on the upstairs porch off the main living room, coffee growing cold, just watching the stream catch the light. The stream’s constant murmur sold me on this lot before we’d graded the house seat. At 2,400 feet, the hardwoods hold onto a coolness the valley below doesn't get, and I trimmed the rhododendron along the bank so I could see our many visitors. I've learned the creek's morning rhythm. Most mornings I’ll see a doe and her fawn pick their way along the far bank. Wild turkeys work the leaf litter past the tree line. Chipmunks scold me from the rock pile, while the songbirds and Carolina wrens fill the air with song. The occasional pileated woodpecker hammering somewhere up the ridge never really stops. It's the kind of quiet during the day that's full, not empty. At night, it's the other kind of quiet. No streetlights, no traffic, with only two homes above my end of the road means the only thing passing by after dark is the occasional set of headlights pulling into a driveway I recognize. Crickets and katydids take over from the birds, an owl calls from somewhere across the stream, and the stars do what they can't do in town. And yet I'm not alone out here, my neighbors in Pinnacle Mountain View are close enough that someone notices if my lights are off too many nights in a row, close enough to call when a tree comes down across the publicly maintained road.
